nl: create a copy of /testbed/hello.php named /testbed/hello-COPY.php
raw: This command copies the file named hello.php from the /testbed directory to a new file named hello-COPY.php in the same /testbed directory.

nl: print the current user's path
raw: This command displays the current values of all the directories listed in your system's PATH environment variable. The PATH variable tells the shell where to look for executable programs when you type a command.

nl: change permissions of /testbed/test.txt to read-only for everyone
raw: This command changes the permissions of the file located at /testbed/test.txt so that the owner, group, and others can only read the file.

nl: list the cron tab
raw: This command lists all the scheduled tasks that are set up to run automatically on your system.

nl: print the max number of user processes
raw: This command shows the maximum number of user processes that a user can run at one time. It displays the current limit for the user you are logged in as.

nl: base64 encode the string 'hello'
raw: This command takes the text "hello" and converts it into a base64 encoded string.

nl: print the installed ssh version
raw: This command displays the version information for the Secure Shell program. It tells you which version of the SSH client or server you are currently using.

nl: list cpu information
raw: This command displays information about the CPU architecture of your system. It shows details like the number of processors and the CPU model.

nl: display network statistics
raw: This command shows you the current network connections and listening ports on your computer. It displays detailed statistics about all active network communication.

nl: find all empty files in the current directory, do not search sub directories
raw: This command searches the current directory for files that are not directories and have no content. It only looks in the current directory and does not look in any subfolders.

nl: print the current working directory
raw: This command tells you the current directory you are in. It prints the full path of the directory you are currently located in.

nl: display the routing table
raw: This command displays the current routing table, which shows how your computer finds the best path to reach different networks.

nl: gzip the file /testbed/hello.php keeping the original file
raw: This command compresses the file located at /testbed/hello.php using the gzip program, and the "-k" flag keeps the original, uncompressed file in the same location.

nl: print current swap usage
raw: This command shows you a list of all the currently active and inactive memory swap partitions on your system.

nl: print the current user
raw: This command tells you the username you are currently logged in as.

nl: display the last 5 lines of the setup_nl2b_fs_1.sh file
raw: This command displays the last five lines of the file named setup_nl2b_fs_1.sh.

nl: print the ip addresses of the system DNS servers
raw: This command reads the contents of the file located at /etc/resolv.conf and then searches that content for any lines containing the text "nameserver".

nl: print the unique lines in setup_nl2b_fs_1.sh
raw: This command finds and displays only the unique lines from the file named setup_nl2b_fs_1.sh.

nl: list all groups on the system
raw: This command queries the system's name service to find information about a specific group. It will show you details about the group you are asking about.

nl: print the current user's umask
raw: This command sets the default permissions for newly created files and directories. It uses a numerical value to control who can read, write, and execute those files.

nl: print lines in the file setup_nl2b_fs_1.sh that contain the characters 'the' and 'a'
raw: This command searches through the file named setup_nl2b_fs_1.sh and then searches the results of that first search for the word "a".

nl: Display the number of sub-directories under /system
raw: This command searches through the directory located at /system for all directories and then counts how many directories it finds.

nl: Display a dump of "/workspace/dir1/long.txt" as floating point values of double size
raw: This command displays the contents of the file located at `/workspace/dir1/long.txt` in a detailed, formatted way. The flag tells the command to use a specific format for showing the data.

nl: Recursively print all files and directories in the '/system/folder2' directory tree including hidden files
raw: This command shows you a graphical, tree-like structure of all files and folders inside the specified system folder. The flag tells the command to include hidden files in the listing.

nl: Recursively finds all files with any cased text "Hello" in the '/system/folder1' folder, and precedes found string with its number in file.
raw: This command searches for the text "Hello" inside all files within the directory located at /system/folder1, and it shows you the line number where it is found.

nl: Print percentage of the space used on the /workspace directory.
raw: This command checks the disk space usage for the `/workspace` directory in kilobytes, then shows only the last line of that output, and finally extracts and displays only the fifth column of that line.

nl: Print the contents of "/workspace/dir1/long.txt" in reverse order
raw: This command reads the contents of the file located at `/workspace/dir1/long.txt`, sorts those lines numerically in reverse order, and then displays only the characters starting from the eighth position of each sorted line.

This command sends a small test message to the device at the IP address 192.168.1.1 to check if it is reachable. The part with the number tells the system to wait only one second for a reply before giving up.

nl: Dump "/system/text1.txt" as ASCII characters
raw: This command displays the contents of the file located at `/system/text1.txt` in a format that is easy to read for character data. The flag specifies that the output should be in a character format.

nl: List all variables (names only) with names containing "H".
raw: This command takes the output of the environment variables and filters them to only show the variable names that start with the letter 'H'.

nl: Remove the last 3 characters from "987654321"
raw: This command takes a number, reverses it, then cuts out a specific section of the reversed number, and finally reverses that section again.

nl: Count all the lines of all files with names ending with 'php' in current directory and subdirectories recursively
raw: This command searches the current directory and all its subdirectories for files that end with the extension "php". It then takes the content of all those found files and counts the total number of lines in that combined output.

nl: Search for the directory "mysql" in the workspace directory.
raw: This command searches through the entire workspace directory for any directories that have the name "mysql".

nl: List all files in the directory /testbed/dir1 and sort them by size in human-readable format
raw: This command lists the files and directories in the specified directory, showing them in a long format with human-readable sizes, sorted by size from largest to smallest.

nl: Find all files in the directory /testbed that have been modified in the last 24 hours and print their path
raw: This command searches the directory named /testbed for files that are regular files and were modified within the last day. It then prints the full path of each file it finds.

nl: Display the sizes and filepaths of all files/directories in /workspace directory sorted in descending order of size
raw: This command calculates the disk usage for every file and directory within the /workspace directory, showing the sizes in a human-readable format. Then, it sorts this list in reverse order based on the size, with the largest items appearing first.

nl: Count all the lines of all php files in the /testbed directory recursively
raw: This command searches through the directory located at /testbed/ for all files ending with the .php extension, then it takes the content of all those files and counts the total number of lines in that combined output.

nl: Remove all *.txt files in '/system' directory but not in it's subdirectories
raw: This command searches the /system directory for any files ending with the .txt extension, only looking in that directory and not in any subfolders. Then, it takes all those found files and deletes them.

nl: print all readline bindings
raw: This command is used to configure the network interface settings, specifically to set the protocol for binding. The flag indicates a specific setting for how network connections are established.

nl: print disk usage of files or folders in /workspace
raw: This command calculates and displays the total disk space used by the contents of the /workspace directory in a human-readable format.

nl: Calculate the md5 sum of the sorted list of md5 sums of all ".py" files under /testbed/dir1/subdir1
bash: find /testbed/dir1/subdir1 -type f -name *.py -exec md5sum {} + | awk '{print $1}' | sort | md5sum
raw: This command searches through the specified directory and its subdirectories for all files ending with the .py extension. It then calculates the MD5 checksum for each of those files and prints only the checksum values in a sorted list. Finally, it calculates the MD5 checksum for those resulting checksums.

nl: Display the 5 smallest files in the /testbed directory and its sub-directories ignoring any empty files.
raw: This command searches the directory named /testbed for files, only looking for regular files, and only those that are larger than zero bytes. It then calculates the size of each of those files and sorts them from smallest to largest, finally showing only the first five smallest files.

nl: Copy all files in the /system directory except those containing 'text' to '/system/folder3/backup_dbg/backup'. Do not include subdirectories.
raw: This command searches the /system directory for files that are not named with "text" and copies each of those found files to the /system/folder3/backup_dbg/backup directory.

nl: Count the *.html files residing in the /testbed directory tree and containing string "foo"
raw: This command searches through all files inside the /testbed directory for any file whose name ends with the extension .html. Then, it takes those found files and searches inside them for the text "foo", only listing the names of the files that contain it. Finally, it counts how many such files were found.

nl: Copy all files and folders below the /testbed directory whose names contain "FooBar" to directory '/testbed/dir3/subdir1/subsubdir1/tmp'
raw: This command searches the directory named /testbed for any files or folders whose names contain "FooBar". It then takes each found item and copies it recursively to the directory located at /testbed/dir3/subdir1/subsubdir1/tmp.

nl: Search for the system host name in "/etc/hosts" and print the IP address in the first awk field
raw: This command searches the file located at the system's configuration directory, specifically the hosts file, for any line containing the system's hostname. Then, it extracts and displays only the first word from the matching line.

nl: move all files in the /workspace folder to / and do not move the files in the sub folder
raw: This command searches the `/workspace` directory for all files and then moves every found file into the current directory.

nl: Counts lines in file /workspace/dir1/a.txt ignoring empty lines and lines with spaces only.
raw: This command reads the file located at `/workspace/dir1/a.txt` and counts the number of non-empty lines, printing the final count at the end.

nl: Find .java files in the testbed directory tree that contain 'Hello', and print their names
bash: find /testbed -name "*.java" -exec grep -Hin Hello {} + | cut -d ":" -f 1 | xargs -I{} basename {}
raw: This command searches through the directory named /testbed for all files ending with the extension .java. Then, it searches inside those files for the text "Hello" and prints the line number and the line itself. After that, it splits each line by a colon and takes only the first part of the split. Finally, it takes those parts and finds the base name of each file.

nl: Count the number of differing lines in "/workspace/dir1/terminate.txt" and "/workspace/dir1/long.txt" with 0 lines of unified context
raw: This set of commands first compares two text files and outputs the differences in a specific format. Then, it filters out any lines that start with the "@" symbol from those differences. Finally, it counts the total number of remaining lines to give you a final number.

nl: Print the total disk usage in bytes of all files listed in "/workspace/files.txt"
raw: This command reads the contents of the file located at `/workspace/files.txt`, then calculates the disk usage in blocks for each line, and finally displays only the last line of that result, showing just the number.

nl: Compute the mean average of the word count of *.txt files in the /testbed directory
raw: This command searches the directory named testbed for all files ending with the .txt extension and then counts the words in each of those files. Finally, it calculates and prints the average number of words per file found.

nl: Remove all files and directories under '/system/folder3/temp' directory tree that match with one of the name patterns '.DS_Store', '._.DS_Store' , '._*', '.TemporaryItems' or '.apdisk'
raw: This command searches through the specified system folder for files matching several specific names, such as those related to macOS temporary files. For every file it finds, it then deletes that file and any subfolders it contains without asking for confirmation.

nl: Compute the MD5 hash of all files under the directory /testbed and store them in a file named hashes.txt in the same directory
raw: This command searches through the directory named /testbed for all files and then calculates a unique digital fingerprint for each file, saving all those fingerprints into a new file called hashes.txt inside the /testbed directory.

nl: Display the contents of textfile3.txt and textfile4.txt side by side, with line numbers and a separator between them.
raw: This command takes the contents of two separate text files, adds line numbers to each one, and then combines those numbered lines into a single output.

nl: Calculate the md5sum of each ".txt" file under "/system" and sort the output.
raw: This command searches the entire system directory for all files ending with the .txt extension and then calculates a unique digital fingerprint for each of those files. Finally, it prints only the digital fingerprints in a sorted list.

nl: Compute the mean average of the word count of *.txt files smaller than 6 words in the /testbed directory
bash: find /testbed -name '*.txt' -print0 | xargs -0 wc -w | awk '$1 < 6 {v += $1; c++} END {print v/c}'
raw: This command searches the /testbed directory for all files ending with the .txt extension and then counts the number of words in each of those files. It finally calculates and prints the average number of words per file for those files that have fewer than six words.

nl: Counts lines in each *.php file in /testbed directory, sorted by number of lines, descending.
raw: This command searches the directory named /testbed for all files ending with the .php extension and then counts the lines in each of those files, finally sorting the results to show the file with the most lines first.

nl: Find the largest 2 directories under /workspace directory
bash: find /workspace -type d -print0 | xargs -0 du | sort -n | tail -2 | cut -f2 | xargs -I{} du -sh {}
raw: This command searches the entire workspace for all directories, then calculates the size of each directory, sorts those sizes from smallest to largest, and finally displays the sizes of the two largest directories.

nl: Remove all *.txt files, except "keep.txt", under /system/folder1 directory modified more than 5 minutes ago. Do not include subdirectories.
raw: This command searches within the specified system folder for files ending in the .txt extension that were modified more than five minutes ago, but it will skip any file named "keep.txt," and then it will delete all the matching files found.
